text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Provincial authorities in the Cuu Long (Mekong) Delta have asked the government to provide more money to combat the effects of floods, which have damaged rice crops for four years in a row.
-- Vietnam and China hope to reach border agreements before 2000.
-- Japan's Deputy Foreign Minister Masahiko Komura has surveyed the implementation of projects funded by Japan's official development assistance during a visit to Ho Chi Minh City.
-- U.S. firms are optimistic about the the Vietnamese market, the Vice President of the Overseas Private Investment Corporation has said.
-- The new National Assembly will convene for its first session on September 18 in Hanoi at the latest to pass an amended National Assembly law and to endorse the appointment of key state positions.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has checked protection measures against flooding in the southern province of Tien Giang, which lies in a lower tributary area of the Mekong River.
-- Vietnam's Pacific Airlines has added a U.S. 1995-model Mcdonnell Douglas MD-82 plane to its fleet.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh has asked the National Committee on AIDS protection to provide the government with details on the identities of carriers of the AIDS virus.
-- 2,284 projects in the cooperatives sector at present have applied for loans amounting to 380.45 billion dong ($35.55 million) for dealing with unemployment.
